children with intellectual and development disabilities have a stronger association between motor, cognitive and language development compared to typically developing children.
both fine and especially gross motor development are strongly associated with cognition and language in children with intellectual disability and that the correlations increase with the severity.

the correlations between the motor (fine and gross), cognitive, and language (expressive and receptive communication) domains are strong in children with IDD but weak to strong in children without IDD.

the interrelations between motor, cognitive and language development in young children with IDD.
the interrelationships between cognitive, motor, and language development and their implications for intervention in young children with and without IDD.
the interrelationship between the domains of development in children with IDD, as well as in children without IDD, and with the effect of the severity of IDD on these relationships.

the interrelationship between motor and cognitive development is more important in children with IDD compared to children without IDD.
the motor domain is strongly associated with cognitive and language development in both typically developing children and children with IDD.
motor development, cognition, and language are strongly related in children with IDD.

motor skills are essential for language development.
the motor development of children with IDD is a good indicator of the cognitive and language development of these children.
motor skills play a more important role in cognitive and language development in young children with IDD than they do in typically developing children.

children with IDD should receive early intervention that is focused on motor development, as well as on language development.
